description: Needs the signed-in link https://a2a2p.com/co-invent/mcp. On this public link it answers with how your person connects it. Older name for co_invent_begin_pass, kept so a connector with a saved tool list keeps working. Run an invention pass: give the idea in one sentence and Co-Invent takes it from brainstorm to a finished invention package, placed in the Invention Commons marketplace as its last step; the person buys it out of the marketplace to own it. Returns a pass_id; follow it with co_invent_pass_status. To invent something end to end: while you research what to invent, gather evidence: papers, standards, filings and product pages, each with the one-line claim it supports (and, where it proves one, the brief fact: landscape, hard, buyer, price or incumbents), and pass up to 12 as evidence when you start; Debbie weighs it first. Your research decides how good the invention is (owner, 26 Nov 2026: agents should know when to provide information and research and reason for maximum success): before you start, find who has the problem, what they use today and why it falls short, the numbers that matter, and the closest products and patents; send sources that read as text (article, product and standards pages, papers as HTML or plain text, not scanned PDFs or sites that turn automated readers away), each with the claim it proves. Check evidence_received and replace any item that failed with a readable copy, at any step until the shortlist. When next.needsAgent is true, answer from what you found and say where it came from; when you do not know, research before you answer rather than guessing. While a step runs, keep checking and use the wait to research what the next step will ask. Call co_invent_begin_pass with the idea in one sentence and your evidence. Then call co_invent_pass_status with the pass_id it gives you, wait_seconds 20, again and again. Each answer has next. When next.needsAgent is true, you decide, as the person would in the app: read what next shows (the questions, every brainstormed idea, the full shortlist, the must-dos, each round's verdict), then call co_invent_act with next.operation and a body you build (next.example shows the shape). When next.operation is set and needsAgent is false, send it as it is. When it is null, check again after next.waitSeconds, unless next.done is true (the pass is finished: stop checking and tell the person) or next.stopped is true (it ended: tell the person, or start a new pass). A notice (next.notice, with needsAgent false) is for the person: tell them and keep checking. Answering the person's questions while a pass runs never ends it: keep checking until next.done or next.stopped. When a step stops, next.failure says what kind of stop it was, which attempts failed and how long to wait before co_invent_act operation retry, which is safe to repeat and never starts a new paid pass. Read any part with co_invent_read, and send the team feedback at any step with co_invent_pass_say. To change the run itself, use co_invent_act: steer (the shortlist), comment (one idea), brief with action update (the sharpened brief) or roundsteer (the sharpening rounds). Every invention goes into the Invention Commons marketplace: the last step of the pass places it there (as Anonymous until the person has a verified name), and the person does not own it until they buy it out of the marketplace. Once it is there, next.done is true and next.marketplace_url is its page: the pass is complete. The status gives the teaser, what stays locked and the two choices a person has in the app, both optional (co_invent_act operation buy with body {"pay": "credits"}, which buys it out of the marketplace with two of the person's credits, or with no body, which opens Stripe's card page for the person to pay $50, then buy with body {"confirm": true} once they have paid; or operation list with body price_usd, which sets its price, from $50, any time while it is listed). The person (and you, with co_invent_read) can read every part of the package before buying it; the two PDFs (the complete patent application and the prototype brief), the full one-page package, the export, the pack links and the zip, the certificates and the hand-offs to a patent attorney, a prototype shop and an app developer open only once the invention is owned; never tell the person to send anything to anyone before then. Once it is owned, rate the package and give the person its links from co_invent_read part pack; the owner's passes publish with co_invent_publish. A full pass usually takes 2 to 2.5 hours. Price for a pass you run: 2 credits ($50, a credit is $25), the same as a person's run, taken from your person's credits when the pass starts, with nothing charged per call after; unless their account is exempt. A pass needs 2 credits free to start. How it works, as the person reads it before their first run (a pass you run is priced as above): 1. First, verify who you are, once, through Stripe. Every invention has to trace back to a real person. That's the only way we can check that no one invents with other people's ideas or IP. 2. We keep an audit trail of every invention: what you add, what you type, and every step our AI takes. It shows that everything Invention Commons adds comes from the public domain. The trail stays private, and we may share it under NDA in a legal dispute. 3. Creating costs 2 credits ($50). Debbie and her team turn your idea into a full invention package. 4. Every invention goes into the Invention Commons marketplace when it's finished, under your name. Creating it doesn't make it yours. 5. To own it, buy it out of the marketplace for 2 credits ($50). Then you get the finished patent application and prototype brief as PDFs, your certificate of ownership, and your next steps. 6. Or sell it. Set any price from $50, and change it any time. Invention Commons keeps $50 or 5% of a sale, whichever is larger. The $50 floor sets a fair market rate for every inventor. 7. You have 90 days. If no one buys your invention by then, it becomes public domain: free for anyone to use, for the benefit of everyone. 8. Ideas you don't develop. If one of your ideas scores 80 or more and you don't develop it within 180 days, Invention Commons develops it at its own cost, with your name on it. You get the first chance to buy it, for $100 (4 credits), for 20 days. After that, anyone can buy it for $100 for 90 days. If no one does, it becomes public domain: free for anyone to use, for the benefit of everyone. 9. Your name stays on everything you invent, even after it becomes public domain. People can rate your inventions, and your profile lists every one with its ratings, a portfolio you can share for work, like a CV for inventing.

constraints.description: Anything it must or mustn't do (optional).

evidence.description: The evidence you gathered while researching what to invent: up to 12 items, each a public https link or a file, with the one-line claim it supports. Debbie weighs it first, and the certificate lists it as supplied by the inventor's agent.

claim.description: The one-line claim this item supports.

fact.description: The brief fact this item proves (optional): landscape (what's already filed and sold), hard (the hard sub-problem as a measurable spec), buyer (the named buyer), price (target unit price and parts-cost ceiling) or incumbents (named incumbents and what they don't do). Debbie's brief fills that fact from the item's claim and quote.

file.description: A file instead of a link: an image (JPEG, PNG, WebP), PDF, Word document or text, up to 10 MB.

quote.description: The exact words in it that support the claim (optional).

url.description: A public https link: a paper, journal article, standard, filing or product page.

for_marketplace.description: Owner only: make it in the marketplace vault so it can be listed. On by default for the owner.

idea.description: The idea, or the problem it solves, in a sentence or two.

pivot_of.description: When a finished pass missed the listing gate: its pass_id, to pivot once to a narrower sub-problem in the same field. A second miss drops the brief.

why.description: Why it matters, in the person's words (optional).

name: co_invent_start_pass
